title: A small bakery's cost table: fixed cost, the profit-maximizing output and the shut-down rule
scenario: Linden Street Bakery sells every bagel at the market price of $3.20, a price it cannot change. The table shows its total cost of baking bagels each morning. The bakery and its numbers are invented, for practice.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the marginal cost of a bagel when output rises from 20 to 30 bagels. Show your work.
parts.sample: MC = change in total cost / change in output = <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>75</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{95 - 75}{30 - 20}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>20</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{20}{10}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math> dollars a bagel.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the bakery's total fixed cost, and explain how the table shows it.

rubric.point: $40, because total cost at zero output is the cost the bakery pays even when it bakes nothing

parts.sample: Total fixed cost is $40. At zero bagels the bakery has no variable cost, so the $40 it still pays is the cost that does not change with output.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Identify the profit-maximizing number of bagels at the market price of $3.20.
parts.sample: The profit-maximizing output is 50 bagels a morning.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain your answer to C(i) using marginal analysis.

rubric.point: Up to 50 bagels each added bagel costs no more than the $3.20 it adds to revenue (MC of $3 between 40 and 50 is below MR = $3.20), while bagels 51 to 60 cost $4 each, more than MR, so producing them lowers profit
accept: the bakery produces where MR = MC, the last output where MR is at least MC

parts.sample: Each bagel adds $3.20 to revenue (MR = P). From 40 to 50 bagels, MC is (150 - 120) / 10 = $3, below MR, so those bagels raise profit. From 50 to 60, MC is (190 - 150) / 10 = $4, above MR, so they would lower profit. The bakery stops at 50, the last output where MR is at least MC.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The market price of bagels falls to $1.60. Explain whether the bakery should keep baking in the short run or shut down, using average variable cost.

rubric.point: Shut down: the lowest AVC in the table is $1.75 (at 20 bagels, $35 ÷ 20), above the $1.60 price, so at every output revenue does not cover variable cost and baking would lose more than the $40 fixed cost
accept: shut down because P = $1.60 is below the minimum AVC of $1.75
shut down: price below AVC at every output

parts.sample: AVC is (TC - 40) ÷ Q: $2.00 at 10 bagels, $1.75 at 20, about $1.83 at 30 and $2.00 at 40, so its lowest value is $1.75. A price of $1.60 is below that, so at any output the bakery would not cover its variable cost: baking 20 bagels, for example, brings in $32 but adds $35 of variable cost. By shutting down it loses only its $40 fixed cost, which is less, so it should shut down in the short run.
